STEP 1 - Scene: A plated meal of salad greens (rocket/arugula-like leaves with some dark leafy greens and a few red bits), three or four small fried or roasted potato pieces, and a portion of crumbed or battered fried fish/chicken pieces with a few herbs. Photographed from above at a slight angle; the plate has sauce smears and crumbs at its edge, suggesting it is mostly eaten.

STEP 2 - Ruler: A square/rounded white plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area = 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Mixed leafy greens (rocket and dark leaves, with some red pepper bits)
- Small roasted potatoes (3 visible pieces, each about 3 cm across)
- Crumbed/battered fried piece (fish or chicken), partly eaten
- Sauce/oil smears on the plate (minor)

STEP 4 - Area (share of 530 cm^2):
- Leafy greens: ~25% = 133 cm^2, height ~2.5 cm, so 330 ml x 0.15 = 50 g x 25 kcal/100g = 12 kcal
- Potatoes: ~6% = 32 cm^2, height ~2 cm, so 64 ml x 0.9 = 58 g... dense starchy pieces, use 0.9 on the tight pile; 58 g x 90 kcal/100g = 52 kcal
- Crumbed fried fish/chicken: ~8% = 42 cm^2, height ~1.2 cm, so 51 ml x 0.9 = 46 g x 230 kcal/100g = 106 kcal
- Sauce/oil residue: ~2 g x 80 kcal/100g = 2 kcal

Food covers roughly 40% of the plate, consistent with a partly eaten meal.

STEP 5 - Volume: Totals above (greens 330 ml, potatoes 64 ml, fried item 51 ml).

STEP 6 - Grams: greens 50 g, potatoes 58 g, fried item 46 g, sauce ~2 g. Total ≈ 156 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: ≈ 12 + 52 + 106 + 2 = 172 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A partly eaten plate of this kind holding about 150 g and roughly 170 kcal is plausible. The greens are light, and the fried item and potatoes carry most of the energy.
